One hundred days before the cap. An exchanger trunk in the lower workings opened and burned
along its whole length, which in a sealed gallery is a matter of minutes rather than hours.
The two members who closed the manual gates did it with their hands and were carried out.

What the survey recorded is that the fire was extinguished by the gallery crew and that the
lower workings were subsequently found flooded, in that order, with no causal claim between
the two clauses. The survey was written by the shift lead who flooded them. It is not a lie
in any sentence; it is a lie in the sequence, and it has held for six years because nobody
who could contradict it wants the workings reopened either.

The burn scars on the steward's hands are from the gates, not from the flooding, and she has
never corrected anyone who assumed otherwise. That is the shape of the woman: she will take
credit for the injury and not for the decision.
